title: KV tiered-hit latency/memory prober and tokens/sec regression detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a deterministic, reproducible prober for evaluating KV prefix cache behavior under tiered hit scenarios. The harness will sweep memory caps, simulated hotset skew, and sequence-length distributions to map hit-rate -> p95 latency -> memory trade-offs and detect tokens/sec regressions. Outputs must integrate with Prometheus dashboards and the nightly regression detector to block releases that increase p95 or drop tokens/sec by >5% on representative workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness that can run locally and in CI with a single binary/script invocation
Metrics exported to Prometheus (prefix: redwood.kv_prober.*) including: tokens_sec, p95_latency_ms, hit_rate, mem_bytes, evictions_per_min
A sweep job that executes three dimensions: memory_limit (4 values), hotset_skew (zipf params, 3 values), sequence_length_mix (short/medium/long), producing a 36-point matrix
Nightly regression job that compares baseline to current and raises an alert if tokens_sec drops >5% or p95 increases >10% for the 90th percentile workload
Dashboard panel with heatmaps for hit_rate vs p95 vs mem_bytes and an artifacts link to raw CSV for each run
test_plan: Workload generator: multi-client async synthetic load with configurable seq_length distribution and token emission rate
Zipf-based key distribution with tunable s parameter to emulate variable hotset concentration
Memory caps simulated with allocator-limited resident set or by configuring runtime cache capacity
Run targets: 50k tokens/sec baseline, scaled down/up to simulate contention; measure steady-state and ramp phases
Measure both per-request p95 and per-shard aggregated p95, collect per-client throughput for tokens/sec stability
implementation_notes: Implement prober in Go to reuse existing runtime client and Prometheus instrumentation libraries
Deterministic RNG seed passed to workload generator to ensure identical key traces across runs
Attach trace IDs to samples so tail-latency correlation with eviction events is possible
Add an export path for raw JSON/CSV artifacts stored in S3: s3://redwood-ci/kvcache-prober/eng-61234/<timestamp>/
Integrate into nightly CI (github-actions 'kvcache-prober-nightly' job) with matrix parallelism for the 36-point sweep
infra_changes: New GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/kvcache-prober.yml (runs on self-hosted runners with GPUs)
Prometheus scrape target registration and Grafana dashboard: dashboard id 'KV Cache Prober (ENG-61234)'
S3 artifact retention policy: store 90 days for raw artifacts and 365 days for baselines
Add alert rule to pagerduty for regression-detected (tokens_sec_drop, p95_increase)
results_summary: Initial local runs show expected correlation: increasing memory cap from 512MB -> 8GB raises hit_rate from 24% -> 78% and reduces p95 from ~120ms -> ~18ms for medium seq mix. Synthetic tokens/sec peaked at 48.6k on the small-hostset skew but degraded under multi-tenant interference simulated by background eviction load. Nightly baseline will be recorded on 2026-03-11.
